A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CalM and retain matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and mouse forecasting/decoding experiments, tokenizer evaluation, component ablations, and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds evaluations on another mouse dataset and C. elegans recordings, preprocessing sensitivity results, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: The NQ tokenizer, dual-axis transformer, embeddings, training objectives, regularizers, and linear/nonlinear decoding heads remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C. Expanded descriptions and additional dataset evaluations do not establish a change to CalM's algorithm.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained simulations and Tseng mouse recordings, v3 evaluates Sun's cue-delay-choice mouse dataset and Atanas's spontaneous activity recordings from freely moving C. elegans. Tables 1–5 add forecasting and position, velocity, and head-angle decoding evaluations, substantially extending populations, recording conditions, and behavioral targets.

E2.justification: The comparator roster is retained, but Appendix B revises the decoding TCN from four causal convolutional layers to four residual blocks containing two weight-normalized convolutions each. This revised comparator appears in Figure 4B and Table 17. Added datasets use the existing POCO and POYO+ comparators.

E3.justification: Added protocols include 64-point Sun trials and a 10/3 mouse split, plus 80-point C. elegans pseudo-trials, a 60/20-session split, and a stated 40-point forecast horizon. TCN decoding changes from 100 to at most 200 epochs, adding early stopping and expanding the weight-decay grid. The smoothing experiment adds controlled preprocessing settings. Appendix B's generic 24-point POCO horizon leaves its C. elegans protocol ambiguous.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused smoothing sensitivity experiment: Table 12 varies EMA alpha across 0.15, 0.60, and 1.00 and measures reconstruction, CalM/POCO forecasting, and decoding. Existing component ablations and PCA/LDA/shuffle analyses are retained; the representation study moves from Appendix E to F.

E5.justification: v1 already includes graphical error bars, some appendix mean-plus-minus values, and shuffle analyses. v3 adds explicit numerical standard deviations for the principal experiments and Wilcoxon tests for multi-session comparisons in Appendix E. These distinguish significant decoding differences from nonsignificant held-out forecasting, with p = 0.3684. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is established.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and 12 add results for new datasets and smoothing conditions; for example, held-out Sun position-decoding R2 is 0.9581 for CalM and 0.8870 for POYO+. Figure 4B replaces TCN pitch/roll/yaw R2 values of 0.4930/0.4188/0.3097 with 0.6217/0.6007/0.6076 under the revised comparator and training settings. Existing CalM benchmark means are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19, including the simulation dynamics, quantization and loss definitions, decoding equations, and d-prime definition, are retained. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows forecasting superiority from 'outperforms strong specialized baselines' to 'achieves competitive performance against' them. The central contributions—shared tokenization, self-supervised pretraining, forecasting/decoding support, and interpretable representations—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 7 explains that trial alignment supplies temporal regularity that may not transfer to spontaneous activity or less structured pseudo-trials. Broader downstream applications are explicitly qualified as untested possibilities. Appendix D newly interprets smoothing sensitivity as affecting reconstruction and forecasting more strongly than decoding.

D1.justification: v3 fills important reproducibility gaps by specifying EMA smoothing with alpha = 0.15, training-split normalization, added dataset selection/windowing, and revised TCN implementation and training details. The abstract replaces a promised code release with a reported release and repository address. The preprocessing additions document previously unspecified procedures; they do not establish that the original experiments changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sun et al. (2025) and Atanas et al. (2023) as dataset sources. Section 2 and the substantive positioning relative to neural foundation models, population dynamics models, and decoding methods remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title now names CalM, headings and grammar are polished, the discussion is expanded, and acknowledgements are added. A numerical-results appendix is inserted and the representation appendix relabeled. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands result presentation with main-text benchmark Tables 1–5, smoothing Table 12, and numerical/statistical Tables 15–19, including difference, p-value, and significance rows. Existing figures are largely retained or relocated. Ablation headers now explicitly identify removed components, and Figure 2's caption is expanded.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence that previously relied on one real dataset, documents consequential preprocessing, tests smoothing sensitivity, strengthens the TCN comparison, and adds statistical assessment of central results. The narrower abstract and expanded limitations better calibrate the claims. The unresolved C. elegans forecasting-horizon description limits that comparison, but the broader validation and improved transparency provide a substantial net quality gain.
